anomalies.observed: R25 (10k) connects the gate net /NET0085 of low-side N-MOSFET T7 (IRLR2905, source on GND) to +3V3. The gate has no pull-down to GND, so with the pre-driver NPN T3 off the gate sits at +3V3 and the switch conducts. The comparable N-MOSFET gate T6 (net /NET0021) is pulled to GND through R19 (10k), which is the usual pattern for a low-side switch.
anomalies.expected: A low-side N-MOSFET gate that must default to off should be pulled down to GND, as on T6 via R19. A pull-up to +3V3 on the gate of a load switch makes the load energise at power-up or when the driver is idle.

evidence.quote: (node (ref "R19") (pin "1") (pintype "passive")) in net GND, with R19 pin 2 on /NET0021 gate of T6

anomalies.impact: The load driven through T7 (the main-pump or ATO load path on H6/D4) may be energised at power-up or while the ESP32 GPIO is idle, which is a safety and control hazard for an irrigation controller.

parsed.summary: The most suspicious item is R25, a 10k pull-up from +3V3 to the gate of low-side N-MOSFET T7 with no pull-down to GND, which would leave the load switch conducting by default. Confidence is moderate because the BT3904 pre-driver topology could make this intentional, and the other connections checked are consistent.
